newsitem.title: USA: Exxon in talks on gas-to-liquids process.
newsitem.headline: Exxon in talks on gas-to-liquids process.

text.p: Exxon Corp Chairman Lee Raymond on Wednesday said the company is holding discussions in about half a dozen areas of the world to promote its proprietary gas-to-liquids technology.

The new technology for converting natural gas to liquid fuel or high-quality feedstock for chemicals and lubes could boost energy use in developing countries with rich natural gas reserves, he said at the company's shareholder meeting.
"The process may prove to be an economic alternative for developing remote gas regions around the world," he said.
An Exxon affiliate recently completed a feasibility study to apply the proprietary technology to develop the offshore Qatar North field, he said.

Raymond also said Exxon, the world's largest integrated oil company, expects no problems in developing its properties in China. The company also expects a smooth transition for its investments in Hong Kong, which will be handed over to the communist regime by Britain in July.
Exxon is currently supplying about 100,000 barrels a day of petroleum products to China, he said.
Asked about the Clinton administration's proposed sanctions on Burma, Raymond said the U.S. policy of imposing unilateral sanctions has put domestic companies at a competitive disadvantage.
